## Item 5 `…f57bc46a3680` — BYPASS, and the text group is a phantom

Flat lime cover, `flat` verdict, background = surface `#b7f38f` (field twin collapse). One text group:
`#b9e0b1`, contrast 7.73, published at RANK 0 on the first attempt with zero refusals — the walk never
had a decision to make.

- Cost of the bypass: 22 of the remaining 25 pool entries are more readable. Best admissible is
  `#34721f` at contrast 64.93 — the text-first rule traded away 57.2 raw APCA.
- Best LEVEL-0 alternative is `#43752e` at 63.06 (rank 1), so the loss is not an artefact of D3's
  salience level; `#34721f` is level 1 (growth 48.7 against a pool median of 0.1227) and sits at rank 17.
- The image ceiling at the node area floor is only 10.77 (`#90e564`): the readable greens are RARE
  triples carried by nodes, not by the residual. Nodes reach what mass cannot — a direct D8 data point.

THE GROUP IS NOT A LINE OF TYPE. 4 members, max pairwise centroid distance 5.14 px against a median
bounding-box height of 29 px: spread/height = 0.177, four centroids inside one glyph. Lane composition
2 L + 1 a + 1 b. This is ONE physical mark named four times — twice in L (chain collapse is per-chain,
not per-object) and once in each chromatic lane (D2 runs collapse per lane, so a mark visible in three
lanes contributes three components). `TEXT_MIN_COMPONENTS` = 4 is satisfied by duplication, and
`collinearity()` returns 0 for a coincident point set by design (`roles/text.ts`: "a group whose glyphs
share a centroid is collinear in the only sense available"), so the coincidence PASSES the collinearity
clause rather than failing it. D2's per-lane graft opened this route; no clause in arm-b 2.4 closes it.

## Item 6 `…d5fd547eb7f3` — CEILING, set by the field and not by the pool

Laminar grey ramp `#646464` -> `#fafafa`. THREE text groups, all geometrically real (24 / 13 / 5 members,
spread-over-height 21.4 / 9.1 / 5.6, all L-lane).

Walk: rank 0 `#727272` (contrast 0.84) and rank 1 `#d1d1d1` (0.94) refused by `I4.below-contrast-floor`;
rank 2 `#515151` (8.65) accepted, 9 attempts. `#515151` IS the admissible pool maximum, and zero pool
entries behind it are more readable — so this is the ceiling, not the walk, even though the walk did
descend. 8 of the top 14 pool entries are refused as twins of the near-white surface.

THE CEILING IS THE RAMP. Contrast is `minRawContrastOverRamp`, the minimum over EVERY point of a ramp
spanning OKLab L 0.45 -> 0.98. Every candidate's lightness is matched somewhere on that line, so the
best achievable by any artwork triple at the area floor is 15.56 (`#3f3f3f`) and by any pixel at all
22.92 (`#272727`). No foreground choice is readable over this field.

CONSEQUENCE: the reviewer's two notes on item 6 have ONE cause. "background should be white" (D10
ruling 2, the polarity defect) and "foreground is hard to read" are both discharged by not publishing
this ramp, or by flipping it — against a flat `#fafafa`, the published `#515151` scores far above the
floor. The readability defect on item 6 belongs to the FIELD stage, not the foreground ranking.
